problem: Video world models predict scene evolution, robot motion, and instruction-driven interaction in one entangled stream, which degrades in long-horizon multi-turn hybrid navigation-manipulation rollouts. No benchmark exists for such hybrid long-horizon world modeling.
motivation: Navigation needs persistent, instruction-agnostic scene consistency, while manipulation needs instruction-conditioned contact dynamics. These are heterogeneous predictive roles that should be modeled separately. The paper asks how to define the world/ego boundary and whether disentanglement is needed.
key_idea: Decompose future embodied video prediction into world and ego states (via a role-conditioned VLM predictor) and generate with a cascade-parallel MoE diffusion model that uses a semantic world-ego mask to route tokens to world/ego experts and unroute them.
insight: Semantic-mask boundaries beat motion (flow) and intention views (EWMScore 61.48 vs 59.36 and 58.69), and full disentanglement (routing and unrouting) beats pre- (58.85), post- (61.09 with proxy, 58.59 without) and none (58.40). The explicit proxy matters, and role-aware components each contribute: neighbor-expanded routing is worth 1.91 points, asymmetric queries 0.98, RCA 0.84. Gains are largest on motion, consistency, and physics metrics.
method: World-ego views: motion (residual optical flow), semantic (robot+manipulated objects = ego mask), and intention (history = world, instruction = ego) boundary definitions.
State predictor: frozen Qwen3-VL-2B with 256 learnable queries (192 world / 64 ego, asymmetric budgets) appended to interleaved instruction/video history.
Role-Conditioned Attention: world queries see the full history but not the current instruction; ego queries see the current instruction and the last K turns only.
CP-MoE generator: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B DiT split into a shared preceding expert (cross-attends to both states) and duplicated world/ego experts, all always active, chunk-wise autoregressive diffusion.
Semantic head + routing/unrouting: a DPT head predicts a world-ego patch mask, routes tokens to experts (with neighbor expansion) and recomposes their outputs.
Training: flow-matching loss plus lambda*(BCE+Dice) mask loss (lambda=0.3, annealed to 20%) with GT masks from BEHAVIOR-1K segmentation.
HTEWorld benchmark: 125K clips (4.5M frames) from BEHAVIOR-1K, 300 multi-turn eval trajectories (2K+ instructions), plus 6 new metrics (RCBD, LPSA, CISR, PMPA, CPDM, FPHS).

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct (frozen state predictor with learned queries) + Wan2.2-TI2V-5B (fine-tuned CP-MoE DiT generator)
setting.training_data: HTEWorld training split: 125K BEHAVIOR-1K simulator clips (4.5M frames) with Gemini-3-flash captions, RAFT flow and simulator segmentation masks; 4 epochs, 16xA100
setting.observation: egocentric RGB video (Galaxea R1 head camera) generated at 480x480, 16 FPS, plus language instructions
setting.action_space: language instructions; outputs video chunks (37 frames/chunk), no robot action output
setting.privileged: GT segmentation-derived world-ego masks used for training supervision only; none at test time

numbers.extra: Fine-tuned on HTEWorld train split; metrics are WorldArena normalized EWMScore and HTEWorld-specific metrics
numbers.evidence: Table hteworld_worldarena and hteworld_specific_metrics: WEM 61.48 EWMScore; 0.31/0.87/0.57/0.54/0.52/0.89

numbers.extra: Same protocol as WorldArena; the training data used for this evaluation is not specified in the text

numbers_note: Not a navigation-task benchmark paper; results are video-generation quality metrics, not SR/SPL. The split label 'test' is assigned by me because the paper does not state an official split name.
results: WEM reaches EWMScore 61.48 on HTEWorld, beating the PAN-style baseline (58.40) by about 3 points and Cosmos-Predict 2.5-14B (55.41) and WoW-7B (53.44) by more, and it leads on all 6 HTEWorld-specific metrics. On original WorldArena it scores 58.10, competitive but below CtrlWorld (59.70) and IRASim (58.12).
limitations: Simulation only (BEHAVIOR-1K); sim-to-real generalization is untested.
Requires instance-segmentation masks for the semantic boundary; the intention/motion views are weaker or noisier.
Autoregressive error accumulation persists over very long horizons; the fixed query budget and general-purpose VLM predictor are not optimal.
